question.text: Which of the following correctly compares the minimum net worth requirements of a Mutual Fund AMC and a Portfolio Management Services (PMS) provider?

answer.text: AMC: Rs. 50 crore; PMS: Rs. 50 crore
AMC: Rs. 50 crore; PMS: Rs. 5 crore
AMC: Rs. 10 crore; PMS: Rs. 25 crore
AMC: Rs. 100 crore; PMS: Rs. 50 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p65), the AMC must have a minimum net worth of Rs. 50 crore. Per NISM PMS workbook (p100), a PMS provider's minimum net worth is Rs. 5 crore. The AMC's higher capital floor reflects its role in managing pooled public money for retail investors. The Trap: Options inflating the PMS minimum to Rs. 25-50 crore or deflating the AMC minimum to Rs. 10 crore are not supported by the workbook references. The Rs. 50 crore vs Rs. 5 crore split is the workbook-anchored pair. Note: AIF Manager regulation is structured around continuing-interest obligations (e.g., Category I/II sponsor or manager continuing interest of 2.5% or Rs. 5 crore whichever is lower; Category III at 5% or Rs. 10 crore) rather than a single AIF Manager net-worth floor, so it is not part of the AMC/PMS net-worth comparison.
